tagline: Peru's port beside the capital, its islands and wildlife just offshore
summary: Callao is Peru's principal port, fused to the southwestern edge of metropolitan Lima and fronting the Pacific beside the historic La Punta peninsula. Offshore lie San Lorenzo — the country's largest island — and the Palomino islets, whose sea-lion colonies already draw wildlife-watching boat tours from the Callao waterfront. Along the metropolitan shore, the Costa Verde cliffs and beaches frame Lima's Pacific frontage from Miraflores to Chorrillos. The open Pacific carries a persistent swell, but the sheltered port approaches and the near-shore islands support passenger movement, and metropolitan Lima's scale and mature ride-hail market anchor the demand. Today the islands and the metropolitan waterfront are served only by tour boats and informal craft — no organised passenger-vessel layer connects them.

transit_planning: Lima's transport investment has centred on the metro and metropolitano BRT; the Pacific frontage and the Callao islands remain served only by tour boats and informal craft. A structured marine layer adds the island and waterfront corridors the land network does not reach.

competitive_landscape: Callao's islands are served by wildlife tour boats with limited sailings, and San Lorenzo has no scheduled access; the Costa Verde frontage has no on-water operator at all. Metropolitan ride-hail is mature on land, but no player bridges the water. The Palomino tours prove near-shore demand; the scheduled, reliable and metropolitan-waterfront gap is wide open.
seasonality: The Peruvian Pacific carries a persistent swell year-round; the austral summer (December–March) offers the warmest, clearest conditions and peak leisure demand, while the grey, humid winter (June–September) softens leisure use. Sheltered port approaches stay workable through the year; exposed Costa Verde legs are swell-gated.
regulatory_note: Peru's maritime passenger operations fall under the Directorate General of Captaincies and Coastguard (DICAPI); island and coastal passenger craft sit within its licensing, coordinated with the Callao port authority given the heavy commercial traffic in the port approaches. San Lorenzo's naval and strategic status means any island landing point requires coordination with the authorities.

precedents.why_it_matters: Existing sea-lion tour demand proves the near-shore corridor and leaves a clear express and reliability gap.
